subject: Outbound address assignment & fallback mapping for private endpoints
messages:
From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@borealis.com>

Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Outbound IPs for private deployment - question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're drafting our firewall/allowlist requirements for a private Redwood deployment inside our VPC and need guidance on a couple of nuanced items before procurement signs off. High level:

- Do you assign a single static egress IP per customer, or do you provide a small contiguous block?
- How do you handle failover across regions / availability zones — do you publish alternate IPs or rely on DNS-weighting?
- We run strict outbound firewalling; can you provide a minimal set of IPs/ports for runtime + control plane + health probes?

Attached is a simple topology diagram of our edge (borealis_network_topology.pdf). We're particularly sensitive to: pinned IPs (for SOC evidence), documented rotation cadence, and a clear fallback map for emergency cutover.

Would appreciate a short mapping table and a sample firewall snippet we can paste into our change request.

Regards,
Paul Chen
Head of Cloud Architecture — Borealis Systems
paul.chen@borealis.com

Subject: Re: Outbound IPs for private deployment - proposed assignment + mapping

Hi Paul — thanks for the topology. TL;DR: we recommend separating runtime egress from control-plane egress, publish a small set of customer-dedicated egress IPs, and provide an explicit fallback IP-range and DNS failover so your firewall change window is predictable. Details below.

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 08:45 AM Paul Chen <paul.chen@borealis.com> wrote:
> Hi Karthik,
> 
> Thanks for taking this. We're drafting our firewall/allowlist requirements for a private Redwood deployment inside our VPC and need guidance on a couple of nuanced items before procurement signs off.

Proposal (high level):
1) Address spaces
   - Runtime egress: we can dedicate 2x /32 public IPs (primary + warm standby) mapped to your customer pool. These are stable for the life of the contract unless an IP rotation is requested.
   - Control plane: separate fixed /32 (or small /28 range if enterprise) so you can allow control-plane telemetry and agent heartbeats separately.

2) Failover approach
   - Primary: traffic egresses via primary IP (A).
   - Warm standby: if primary host or AZ degrades, traffic switches to standby IP (B) on the same pool.
   - Regional failover: we publish a region-level fallback (C) and provide DNS-weighted records for flows that tolerate short TTL-based shifting. For strict-firewall environments you should allow the fallback IP(s) so we can fail over without last-minute change requests.

3) Operational controls
   - mTLS between your proxy and our runtime for identity assertion (recommended).
   - Optional outbound proxy (customer-owned) — if you require full egress control, route runtime egress to your proxy; we will keep a small set of egress destinations and support mTLS to your proxy.

4) Artifacts
   - I attached a rough mapping table (egress-assignment-table.xlsx) with primary/standby/fallback IPs for the PoC.
   - We'll provide a short playbook (egress-fallback-playbook.md) that lists the steps and expected time-to-failover.

Sample firewall lines you can paste into a change ticket:
   - ALLOW TCP 443 to 34.203.12.45/32  # runtime-primary (Redwood)
   - ALLOW TCP 443 to 34.203.12.46/32  # runtime-standby
   - ALLOW TCP 443 to 52.12.78.90/32   # control-plane (Redwood telemetry)
   - ALLOW UDP 53 to 8.8.8.8/32        # DNS (if not using internal resolver)

Next steps: 30-min sync to confirm IPs and lock change window. I have availability Wed 11/3 9:00-11:00 or Thu 11/4 14:00-15:00 PT.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Outbound IPs - ops and rotation notes

Karthik / Paul — adding a few operational items we consistently see missed during signoff: 

- Rotation policy: if you want cryptographic rotation (for e.g., ephemeral certs or IP reclamation), define a rotation window and a notification cadence. We support scheduled rotations with a 7-day advance notice and automated announcement to your ops channel.
- Tagging & ownership: each egress IP we assign will be tagged in our console with the customer_id and region; use that for audit queries.
- Telemetry & evidence: control plane connections are logged at token-level and archived for 90 days by default (longer retention is an add-on). We can produce an evidence bundle for procurement (connection timelines and NAT mappings).

Sample firewall/ACL snippet (for your change request):
   - Egress allow list (production):
     * 34.203.12.45/32  tcp:443  # redwood-runtime-us-west1-primary
     * 34.203.12.46/32  tcp:443  # redwood-runtime-us-west1-standby
     * 52.12.78.90/32   tcp:443  # redwood-controlplane-us-west1
     * 52.12.78.91/32   tcp:443  # redwood-controlplane-us-west1-standby
     * 3.5.6.7/32       udp:53   # optional external DNS

Operational notes: set firewall rules with a tag/note referencing the RFC/change ID so future rotations and audits are traceable. If you need signed evidence for the IP assignment (for procurement), we'll hand over the signed allocation letter and the last-rotation manifest.

Laura Bennett
Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

If we can get the short checklist and exact IPs before Friday EOD we can lock the firewall window for next week.

Thanks,
Paul

Paul — looping in a short checklist and the playbook excerpt below. We can produce a signed allocation letter once you confirm PoC scope and billing account.

FINAL MAPPING (PoC)
- runtime-primary: 34.203.12.45/32
- runtime-standby: 34.203.12.46/32
- controlplane-primary: 52.12.78.90/32
- controlplane-standby: 52.12.78.91/32
- dns: allow UDP 53 to 8.8.8.8/32 or use your internal resolver

EVIDENCE CHECKLIST (attach to procurement)
- Signed IP allocation letter (we will provide)
- Mapping table (egress-assignment-table.xlsx)
- Playbook excerpt (egress-fallback-playbook.md) with RTO/RPO expectations
- Contact for emergency IP rotation: network-ops@redwood.com (24/7 pager)

PLAYBOOK EXCERPT (condensed)
1) Automatic failover (within region): primary -> standby switch occurs automatically if the runtime host signals degraded health (expected switchover < 90s). No firewall change required if standby is already allowed.
2) Regional fallback: manual trigger by Redwood ops if region-level outage detected. Expected time-to-failover: 10-30 minutes (DNS TTL, BGP propagation as applicable). Recommend you allow the region-level fallback IPs in the change window to avoid last-minute changes.
3) Post-failover evidence: RFC + NAT mapping logs and token-level telemetry are packaged and sent to your security contact within 2 hours of failover event.

SAMPLE FIREWALL RULES (apply to your outbound ACL)
- allow tcp 443 to 34.203.12.45/32  # runtime-primary
- allow tcp 443 to 34.203.12.46/32  # runtime-standby
- allow tcp 443 to 52.12.78.90/32  # controlplane-primary
- allow tcp 443 to 52.12.78.91/32  # controlplane-standby
- allow udp 53 to 8.8.8.8/32     # public DNS (optional)

Next steps: if this looks good we will: (1) create & sign the allocation letter, (2) lock the firewall window with your SRE, (3) schedule a 30-min hands-on run-through during the change window. Karthik will own the implementation coordination.

—Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
